description.narrative: Number of CSO members engaging in the formal or informal peace architecture (M/W/B/G)

comment.narrative: 100 CSO members engaging in the formal or informal peace architecture 50 of trained CSOs

As the number of CSO members engaged in formalinformal peace architecture will be measured in the endline survey at the end of the project Geneva Call conducted an interim follow up with organisations which have participated in training. Six of the trained civilian organisations have begun to take action to share their knowledge with others to improve the protection of civilians and compliance of armed actors with IHLIHRL. The Karenni National Womens Organisation posted on Facebook Annex 5 following their training on IDPs on the importance of taking action against those who commit serious violations against women. Following the training a participant from Kayahli Phu Youth Organisation shared back the learnt knowledge to our families and those we communicate with whenever we get a chance regarding the messages of IHL.One participant from the Kachin Baptist Convention stated that The participants remind their friends not to wear use military related clothing materials when they go out and travel as they can be mistakenly considered as someone from parties to conflict and targeted.A Field Liaison from the Karen Human Rights Group noted After receiving training from GC I know more about IHL. We can now explain in more detail information to soldiers after receiving training from GC. By working with GC we can better promote IHL. We see human rights violations in the field by soldiers in the area operating in Karen State and it motivates me to fix these. It is helpful that we use GCs two Deeds of Commitments and other training materials provided by GC during the training as we share these with soldiers during the training.A participant from the Karen Information Centre highlighted that they have shared the information with those who were not able to join the training such as our Citizen Journalists reporters and field reporters. We shared with them what they should know when collecting information. A village youth leader who attended a community workshop in Deemawso township noted that they shared the messages about what is violent or is breaking the rules of IHL. We also shared the post about the protection of civilians. We do have more conversations in person as here in our place there is no internet connection at all.
